notes.shape: 13 topic domains plus `behavior`. Both mappers returned 14 domains; 11 lined up. The three that did not were cut differently: supply had assets, funding, and org; demand had xlm, rwa, and ecosystem. The merged set keeps supply's assets (it now holds stablecoins and real-world assets, so demand's rwa domain and both payments domains' asset leaves moved in), keeps funding, and joins org and xlm as ecosystem. The two payments domains were the nearest thing to a catch-all: their asset leaves went to assets, their anchor and ramp leaves joined standards, and institutional adoption went to ecosystem. Thirteen rather than twelve: folding ai into tooling, or funding into ecosystem, would have made a catch-all. Leaf ids follow `<domain>.<slug>`; a scope's Out clause names the leaf that holds what it leaves out.
notes.method: Supply had 160 leaves and demand 172. Each mapper leaf was placed into exactly one merged leaf, split across named leaves, or dropped with a reason; a build script checked that none was left out. Leaves that test the same knowledge merged, and the facets list carries what each mapper's separate leaf asked. A leaf that one question could not cover was split. A leaf from one mapper stayed when its evidence showed demand (a named persona, real questions) or risk (lost funds, a broken build, a stale name). eval/qa/corpus and audit/*.json were not read before taxonomy.json was first written.
notes.weightStandard: 3 = an agent meets it constantly, or a wrong answer loses funds or breaks a build. 2 = regular. 1 = niche but real. Applied across the whole map, not per domain. Where the mappers were one step apart the standard decided, and weightReason says why. Cases: weight 3 gets 2 or 3, weight 2 gets 1 or 2, weight 1 gets 1; cases equals the number of facets, and 3 is used only for three clearly separate facets. A topic that analysts ask often but where a wrong answer costs nothing beyond the answer (TVL rankings, metrics, institutional adoption) is weight 2 with a dated-and-sourced test, not weight 3.
